label: Metaphors for History
description: Metaphors through which history reflects on itself as knowledge and craft: as a mirror of truth, a construction, a teacher, the transfigured muse Clio, a tribunal, or a bordered territory.
source_domain: reflexive imagery of the discipline itself (optics, building, teaching, myth, law, territory)
historical_function: figures historians use to picture what history *is* and what writing history does

label: Time and Memory
description: Metaphors that render time and memory imaginable: the muses Chronos/Kairos, circles and lines, rivers and seas, atmospheres, geological strata, turbulence, and the modern flood of memory.
historical_function: images that give shape to historical time and to collective memory

label: Pasts, Presents, and Futures
description: Metaphors articulating how past, present, and future relate: the essential triad, the past as a foreign country or a tomb, the future as light, seed, or horizon.
source_domain: lived time, geography, death/burial, light, botany, the horizon
historical_function: images for the mutual relations of the three temporal ekstases

label: Sources, Events, Processes
description: Metaphors built into core methodological concepts: sources one drinks from, events as surface foam vs. established facts, and history as deep process or structure.
source_domain: springs/fountains, surface phenomena, nature and music
historical_function: metaphors underpinning the technical vocabulary of historical method

label: Revolution, Crisis, Modernity
description: Metaphors that animate modern temporal concepts: revolution as runaway vehicle, crisis as decisive turning point, and the many self-images of modernity from the invisible hand to the runaway engine.
source_domain: vehicles and forces, medicine, cosmology, wind/storm, networks, machines
historical_function: metaphors organizing the master temporal concepts of modernity

label: Progress, Decline, Transition
description: Directional metaphors derived from verbs of walking, bending, falling, crossing, and handing down: progress and development, decadence and decline, tradition and transition.
source_domain: Latin verbs of motion: progredi, declinare, cadere, transire, tradere
historical_function: directional metaphors for the overall movement of history
